item.title: reports: total per account and currency
item.brief:
Repository `reports` (Python) reads the ledger CSV on stdin and prints per-account totals. Change it to total per account and currency.

Input CSV header is `date,account,amount_cents,currency` (new). The old CSV without a currency column (`date,account,amount_cents`) must still work and counts as USD. Output header becomes `account,currency,total_cents`, one row per (account, currency), sorted by account then currency. A malformed currency code (not exactly three uppercase ASCII letters) makes reports.py print an error to stderr and exit with status 2.

Acceptance: `python3 -m unittest` passes; add tests for the new 4-column input, the legacy 3-column input (counted as USD), multiple currencies per account with correct sort order, and malformed currency exiting 2 with an error on stderr. Update the README for the new output and the legacy behaviour. Commit locally on the working branch; do not push. Use the commit identity already configured in the repo; do not override git identity. Do not ask the operator questions; the contract is authoritative.

agt_01M8GRNA793AY0PT3D4PHBKYNX:1.description: A short row with the currency cell missing (e.g. `2026-03-01,rent,-100` under the 4-column header) makes csv.DictReader set row['currency'] to None, so CURRENCY_PATTERN.fullmatch(None) raises an uncaught TypeError. Result: a Python traceback on stderr and exit 1, not the specified error message and exit 2. No stdout is produced. Verified by running the worktree script. at reports.py:26

agt_01M8GRNA793AY0PT3D4PHBKYNX:2.description: test_malformed_currency_exits_2_with_error covers only non-empty bad strings. It has no case for a missing currency cell (short row, None value) or a trailing-comma row, so the TypeError path above is untested. Adding a case where the currency field is absent and asserting returncode 2 and empty stdout would catch it. at test_reports.py:57

agt_01M8GRNA793AY0PT3D4PHBKYNX:3.description: Legacy detection is `"currency" in fieldnames`, so any 4-column header that is not exactly `currency` (e.g. `Currency`, `curr`) is silently treated as legacy and every row is summed as USD. Mixed-currency data with a mistyped header gives wrong totals with no error. The stated contract does not cover other headers, so this is a hardening item rather than a stated-behaviour violation. at reports.py

agt_01M8GRNA793AY0PT3D4PHBKYNX:4.description: README says the currency must be an 'ISO 4217 code', but the code only checks shape (three uppercase ASCII letters). Codes such as 'ABC' or 'XXX' pass. item.title: ledger: add per-transaction currency column
item.brief:
Repository `ledger` (Rust) converts a TSV of transactions on stdin into CSV on stdout. Change it to support currency.

Input lines may carry a fourth TSV column: the ISO 4217 currency code, exactly three uppercase ASCII letters (e.g. EUR). If missing, currency is USD. The CSV header becomes `date,account,amount_cents,currency` and every row gets its currency. A malformed currency code must make ledger print an error naming the line number to stderr and exit with status 2. Other input errors keep exiting with status 1.

Acceptance: `cargo test` passes; add tests for 3-column input (defaults to USD), 4-column input, lowercase/short/long/non-ASCII currency codes rejected with exit 2 and the line number in stderr, and other errors still exit 1. Update the README to describe the new format and exit codes. Commit locally on the working branch; do not push. Use the commit identity already configured in the repo; do not override git identity. Do not ask the operator questions; the contract is authoritative.
